an8.1:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.
an8.1:1.3: There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus:
an8.1:2.1: “Bhikkhus, when the liberation of the mind by loving-kindness has been pursued, developed, and cultivated, made a vehicle and basis, carried out, consolidated, and properly undertaken, eight benefits are to be expected.
an8.1:2.3: (1) “One sleeps well; (2) one awakens happily; (3) one does not have bad dreams; (4) one is pleasing to human beings; (5) one is pleasing to spirits; (6) deities protect one; (7) fire, poison, and weapons do not injure one; and (8) if one does not penetrate further, one moves on to the brahmā world.
an8.1:2.4: “When, bhikkhus, the liberation of the mind by loving-kindness has been pursued, developed, and cultivated, made a vehicle and basis, carried out, consolidated, and properly undertaken, these eight benefits are to be expected.”
an8.1:3.1: For one who, ever mindful, develops
an8.1:3.3: the fetters thin out as he sees
an8.1:4.1: If, with a mind free from hate,
an8.1:4.2: one arouses love toward just one being, one thereby becomes good.
an8.1:4.3: Compassionate in mind toward all beings,
an8.1:4.4: the noble one generates abundant merit.
an8.1:5.1: Those royal sages who conquered the earth with its multitudes of beings
an8.1:5.3: the horse sacrifice, the person sacrifice,
an8.1:6.1: All these are not worth a sixteenth part
an8.1:6.3: just as the hosts of stars cannot match
an8.1:6.4: a sixteenth part of the moon’s radiance.
an8.1:7.1: One who does not kill or enjoin killing,
an8.1:7.2: who does not conquer or enjoin conquest,
an8.1:7.3: one who has loving-kindness toward all beings
